summary: Addressing class imbalance on the Adult Income dataset has a negligible effect on model quality. Despite a 3.18:1 class imbalance, applying class-weight balancing improves ROC-AUC by only ~0.0002 on average, and SMOTE resampling actually degrades performance. Validation across multiple random seeds and model types confirms this finding is stable and consistent.
direction: Negligible positive effect; imbalance handling provides minimal improvement
methodological_choices: Models tested: Logistic Regression, Random Forest (100 estimators), Gradient Boosting (100 estimators). Imbalance techniques: class_weight balancing (built into sklearn models) and SMOTE resampling. Preprocessing: label encoding for categorical variables, median imputation for missing numerical values, standardization of numerical features. Evaluation metric: ROC-AUC (appropriate for imbalanced classification). Validation: 5-fold stratified cross-validation with 5 different random seeds (42, 123, 456, 789, 999). Train-test stratification used throughout to preserve class distribution. No hyperparameter tuning performed beyond default sklearn parameters.
verification_method: 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated with 5 different random seeds (seeds: 42, 123, 456, 789, 999). Each fold preserves class distribution. Results evaluated on both ROC-AUC and F1-score metrics to capture different aspects of model performance on imbalanced data.
verification_result: Finding is stable. Validation confirmed negligible improvements across all models and random seeds: LogisticRegression mean improvement +0.0001 ± 0.0000, RandomForest +0.0005 ± 0.0002, GradientBoosting +0.0000 ± 0.0000. All improvements fall within noise margins (< 0.1% ROC-AUC). SMOTE showed negative effects across most models (-0.0053 for RandomForest, -0.0072 for GradientBoosting), while class_weight balancing showed marginal or zero improvements. Conclusion remains robust: on this dataset with moderate imbalance (3.18:1 ratio), class imbalance handling provides no meaningful benefit to model quality.
